diagnostic_evidence.quote: then at least for some neighborhood $\mathcal O \subset \caC_n$ (which depends on $\omega$) of $Y_*$ the corresponding iteration map
it cannot be guaranteed that positive definite matrices are generated

issues.failure_explanation: The paper asserts that S_omega is defined on all of C_m x O, where O is only a neighborhood of Y_* in C_n. For omega>1 the first component (1-omega)X+omega S_1(Y) is not positive definite for arbitrary X in C_m. For example, X=tI with t large gives an indefinite matrix, so S_2 of it is undefined. The paper itself says positive definiteness cannot be guaranteed for omega>1. Well-definedness needs a neighborhood of (X_*,Y_*) in both variables, not only of Y_*. The conclusion that S_omega is defined near the whole orbit is then derived from this wrong domain.

failure_location.quote: is well defined as a map from $\caC_m \times \mathcal O$ to $\caC_m \times \caC_n$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that S_omega is well defined on a neighborhood O of (X_*,Y_*) in C_m x C_n. Then extend to a neighborhood of the whole orbit by the equivariance (eq: orbital equivariance relaxation).
issues.overall_effect: Only the stated domain of S_omega is wrong. Lemma equal derivatives and the local theorem correctly use a neighborhood of (X_*,Y_*), so no formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Euclidean overrelaxation map claimed well defined on C_m x O, but positive definiteness of X_{t+1} fails for omega>1
issues.why_classification: A short local change of the domain statement suffices. All later claims are already phrased for a neighborhood of the fixed point.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking the trace of sum x~_i x~_i^T = I_n gives sum ||x~_i||^2 = n. The stated constraint ||x~_i||_2 = n/k then forces n^2/k = n, i.e. n=k. For the experiment's n=50, k=55 the stated frame scaling problem has no solution, so it cannot be equivalent to the (solvable) operator scaling problem. The operator-scaling equations give l_i^2 ||R x_i||^2 = 1/k and sum l_i^2 (R x_i)(R x_i)^T = I/n. These yield ||x~_i||^2 = n/k with x~_i = sqrt(n) l_i R x_i, so alpha_i = sqrt(n) l_i. The stated alpha_i = n l_i^2 does not give the frame normalization sum x~_i x~_i^T = I_n.

failure_location.quote: So $P = R$ and $\alpha_i = n\ell_i^2$ yield a solution to frame scaling, and vice versa.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the norm condition as ||x~_i||_2^2 = n/k. Replace the correspondence by alpha_i = sqrt(n) l_i, i.e. alpha_i^2 = n l_i^2.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalence between frame scaling and the operator scaling instance is not correct as written, so the description of the frame-scaling experiment is unreliable. No formal theorem is affected.
issues.title: Frame-scaling formulation inconsistent and not equivalent to the stated operator scaling problem
issues.why_classification: The correct formulation follows from the displayed operator-scaling equations by a short routine computation. The experiment and all theorems are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that the CP map $\Phi$ is positivity improving

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem local convergence, and Lemma null space of Hessian on which it relies, require Phi to be positivity improving. For the frame-scaling map with A_i = e_i x_i^T, Phi(vv^T) = diag((x_i^T v)^2). This is singular whenever v is orthogonal to some x_i, and such v != 0 exists since n>=2. Equivalently, w=e_1 and v orthogonal to x_1 give w^T A_i v = 0 for all i. So the hypothesis of the theorem is violated, and the one-dimensional null space and the formula rho(omega) are not established for this instance. The experiment can only be consistent with the theorem, not validate it.

failure_location.quote: validating the local convergence result in Theorem~\ref{thm: local convergence}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to say the observations are consistent with the theory heuristically, noting the frame-scaling map is not positivity improving. Alternatively prove the Hessian null-space property for this map.
issues.overall_effect: The statement that the experiment validates the local rate theorem overreaches. The theory does not cover the main experimental application, so the observed speedup there is not backed by the stated guarantees.
issues.title: Frame-scaling experiment is claimed to validate Theorem local convergence although its CP map is not positivity improving
issues.why_classification: Rewording the claim resolves it without changing any theorem or the empirical results. The paper already notes that the algorithm is used in practice without checking such assumptions.
